name: New Mexico
agencyName: New Mexico Motor Vehicle Division (Taxation and Revenue)

retake.waitBetweenAttempts: Retake typically allowed after a short wait; confirm with your MVD field office
retake.retakeFee: May require a new test fee on additional attempts

gdl.nightCurfew: No driving midnight-5 a.m. on a provisional license (with exceptions)
gdl.passengerLimits: No more than one passenger under 21 on a provisional license (with exceptions)

requiredDocuments: Proof of identification number (e.g. Social Security card)
Proof of identity and age (e.g. certified birth certificate or U.S. passport)
Two proofs of New Mexico residency (for a REAL ID)
Proof of enrollment or graduation (applicants under 18)
process.realIdNotes: A New Mexico REAL ID requires proof of identity, proof of your identification/Social Security number, and two documents proving New Mexico residency. A non-REAL ID (standard) credential is also offered.
process.visionStandard: At least 20/40 in one or both eyes, with or without corrective lenses

facts.pointSuspensionThreshold: 12 points in 12 months triggers a one-year suspension; 7 or more points may lead to a hearing
facts.moveOverRule: Move over a lane or slow down for stopped emergency, police, and highway maintenance vehicles displaying flashing lights
facts.schoolZoneSpeed: 15 mph in a marked school zone during posted hours (unless otherwise posted)

bacAdult.display: It is unlawful to drive with an alcohol concentration of 0.08 or more (or while under the influence of intoxicating liquor).

citation.label: Driving under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs

bacUnder21.display: A driver under 21 with an alcohol concentration of 0.02 or more loses driving privileges under the implied consent act.

citation.label: Grounds for revocation of license; alcohol concentration thresholds

bacCommercial.display: A commercial vehicle driver with an alcohol concentration of 0.04 or more commits driving under the influence.

citation.label: Driving under the influence; commercial motor vehicles

impliedConsentRefusal.display: Refusal to submit to chemical testing revokes the license for one year (or until reinstatement conditions are met). Refusal is not a separate crime, but refusing after a DWI arrest supports an aggravated DWI charge.

citation.label: Refusal to submit to chemical tests; revocation

openContainerProhibited.display: It is unlawful to drink or possess an open container of alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a motor vehicle on a public highway.

citation.label: Consumption or possession of alcoholic beverages in open containers in a motor vehicle prohibited

duiFirstSuspensionDays.display: On a first DWI conviction the division must revoke the driving privilege for one year.

citation.label: Mandatory revocation of license by division

conditions.detail: rural interstate highways posted at 75 mph

ruralInterstateMaxMph.display: The statutory maximum speed is 75 mph, and 75 mph is the highest posted limit on rural interstates.

conditions.detail: urban interstate highways posted at 75 mph

urbanInterstateMaxMph.display: Maximum posted speed limit on urban interstates is 75 mph, the statutory ceiling under NMSA 1978, § 66-7-301(A)(4).

citation.label: IIHS maximum posted speed limits by state (July 2026)
citation.citation: IIHS, Maximum posted speed limits (New Mexico: 75 mph rural and urban interstates)

conditions.detail: business or residence district, absent a different posted limit

residentialDefaultMph.display: 30 mph in a business or residence district (55 mph on an unposted county road).

conditions.detail: only where the school zone is properly posted
while children are going to or leaving school

schoolZoneMph.display: 15 mph when passing a school while children are going to or leaving school and the school zone is properly posted.

basicSpeedLaw.display: Speed must be controlled as necessary to avoid collisions and to account for conditions, and no person may drive at a speed greater than is reasonable and prudent.

rightTurnOnRed.display: After stopping at a steady red signal a driver may turn right unless a sign prohibits the turn.

leftTurnOnRedFromOneWay.display: A left turn on a steady red signal from a one-way street into a one-way street is permitted after stopping, unless prohibited by sign.

seatBeltEnforcement.display: Safety belt use is enforced as a primary offense: the safety belt and child restraint requirements are enforced whether or not another statute is being enforced.

citation.label: Enforcement programs (safety belt and child restraint enforcement)

conditions.detail: commercial motor vehicle drivers are separately banned from handheld use under NMSA 1978, § 66-7-375

handheldPhone.display: New Mexico has no statewide handheld phone ban for ordinary drivers; only commercial motor vehicle drivers are barred from handheld use (several municipalities impose local bans).

citation.label: Use of a handheld mobile communication device while driving a commercial motor vehicle

texting.display: No driver may read, view or manually type a text message on a handheld mobile communication device while driving.

moveOver.display: Approaching a stationary emergency, recovery, repair or maintenance vehicle displaying flashing lights, a driver must change to a non-adjacent lane if possible, or otherwise slow to a safe speed.

citation.label: Operation of vehicles on approach of authorized emergency vehicles; stationary vehicles

headlightsRequired.display: Lighted lamps are required from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise and whenever visibility is insufficient; New Mexico has no statutory wipers-on headlight rule.

parkFtFromHydrant.display: No stopping, standing or parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.

citation.label: Stopping, standing or parking prohibited in specified places

conditions.detail: crosswalk at an intersection; parking on a crosswalk is prohibited entirely

parkFtFromCrosswalk.display: No parking on a crosswalk, or within 20 feet of a crosswalk at an intersection.

citation.label: Stopping, standing or parking prohibited in specified places

parkFtFromStopSign.display: No parking within 30 feet upon the approach to a flashing beacon, stop sign or traffic-control signal at the side of a roadway.

citation.label: Stopping, standing or parking prohibited in specified places

parkFtFromRailroad.display: No parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail of a railroad crossing.

citation.label: Stopping, standing or parking prohibited in specified places

pointSystem.display: The Motor Vehicle Division maintains a point system and suspends licenses on point accumulation.

pointSuspension.display: Accumulating 12 or more points within a 12-month period results in license suspension (12 points: up to a 12-month suspension; 7 to 10 points draws a warning letter).

permitMinAgeMonths.display: An instruction permit may be issued at 15 years of age to a student enrolled in or who has completed an approved driver education course.

permitHoldingMonths.display: The instruction permit must be held at least six months before a provisional license is issued at 15 years 6 months (30 days is added for each traffic violation committed while on the permit).

supervisedHoursTotal.display: The practice driving component requires at least 50 hours of actual driving by the applicant.

supervisedHoursNight.display: At least 10 of the 50 practice driving hours must be night driving (waivable for documented low night vision).

gdlNightCurfew.display: A provisional licensee may drive only between 5:00 a.m. and midnight unless accompanied by a licensed driver 21 or older or covered by a work, school, family, medical or emergency exception.

gdlPassengerPhase1.display: A provisional licensee may carry no more than one passenger under 21 who is not an immediate family member.

minLiability.display: Evidence of financial responsibility requires at least $25,000 per person / $50,000 per accident for bodily injury and $10,000 for property damage.

citation.label: Evidence of financial responsibility; amounts and conditions

crashReportThresholdUsd.display: A written accident report is required for a crash causing bodily injury, death, or apparent property damage of $500 or more.
